summary: This photooxidation reaction involves singlet oxygen generation and [4+2] cycloaddition using methylene blue as the photocatalyst (0.9 mol%) under 700 nm LED irradiation in CD3CN solvent. The continuous-flow photoreactor utilized PFA tubing with a 4.6 mL reactor volume, 16-minute residence time, and operated under 10 bar back-pressure with pressurized air. The batch process suffered from poor oxygen solubility and limited light penetration, achieving only 23% yield after 30 minutes. Flow chemistry dramatically improved the reaction outcome by enabling pressurized air introduction for better mass transfer, uniform light exposure throughout the reactor, and continuous operation, resulting in 96% yield - a remarkable 73 percentage point improvement over batch conditions.

chemistry.scope_summary: Wide range of phenolic substrates converted to benzoquinones and p-quinols. Electron-rich phenols (e.g., methoxyphenols) gave excellent yields. Unsubstituted phenol and electron-deficient phenols remained unreacted. Method also works for naphthols and produces vitamin precursors like trimethylbenzoquinone (vitamin E precursor) and menadione (vitamin K3).

summary: This photocycloaddition reaction utilizes triplet sensitization with 2,2'-dimethoxythioxanthone (2,2'-MeOTX) as the photocatalyst at 1 mol% loading under 455 nm COB LED irradiation. The flow process operates in acetonitrile at 200°C with a 5-minute residence time and 6.0 mL/min flow rate using a FlowSyn steel coil reactor (30 mL volume) equipped with a 34 bar back-pressure regulator. Flow chemistry enabled daisy-chaining of the initial photochemical step with high-temperature thermal cascade reactions, dramatically improving yield from 16% in batch (2 hours) to 88% in flow with a 24-fold intensification factor. The high-temperature operation required for the thermal cascade was much safer to implement in the continuous flow reactor compared to batch processing.

summary: This photocatalyzed radical addition employs 2-benzopyrylium intermediates generated in situ as the photoredox catalyst under 450 nm LED irradiation. The flow process operates in a 1.0 mL photochemical reactor using 1,2-dichloroethane as solvent at room temperature (25°C) with a 2.5 minute residence time and 24.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 77% yield. In contrast, the batch baseline required elevated temperature (50°C) and 60 minutes reaction time to obtain 76% yield. Flow processing provided a 24-fold intensification in reaction rate while maintaining comparable yield and enabling safer room temperature operation, demonstrating superior scalability for this photoredox transformation.
